title: Identify tote rack centering features (little feet and side fins) and their purpose
summary: Visually identify the tote rack centering mechanisms in the OptiSweep tote-on-cylinder area: the tote sits on the cylinder, the rack’s “little feet” align the tote to the center when it drops, and the side “fins” help move packages toward the center after off-center impacts.
when_to_use: Use when you need to confirm (by visual inspection) that the tote rack hardware includes the centering features described for tote drops: tote-on-cylinder positioning, little feet for center alignment, and side fins for centering after off-center hits.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for troubleshooting RMS/WCS/SSMS/API faults; this runbook is limited to visual identification of tote rack hardware features.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Perform the on-site visual inspection of the tote rack/tote-on-cylinder hardware and describe the centering features (little feet and side fins) and their intended purpose.

access_or_tools_needed: Visual access to the tote rack/tote-on-cylinder hardware

system_preconditions: Tote rack hardware is physically accessible for visual inspection.

visual_references.description: Training frame showing the tote rack/tote-on-cylinder area and describing: tote sits on the cylinder; little feet align tote to center on drop; side fins move packages toward center if they hit off-center; includes building vs Hazlett drop severity note.

steps.title: Locate the tote rack area described in the tote-on-cylinder hardware
steps.purpose: Establish the correct physical area to inspect for the centering mechanisms.
steps.instruction: Visually locate the tote rack area where the tote sits on the cylinder (the tote-on-cylinder position).
steps.expected_result: You can point to the tote-on-cylinder area of the tote rack (the location where the tote sits on the cylinder).
steps.healthy_condition: The tote rack area is identifiable as the cylinder seating location for the tote.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the tote-on-cylinder seating area to inspect for the described centering features.

actions.label: Visually locate tote-on-cylinder area
actions.exact_action: Locate the tote rack area where the tote sits on the cylinder.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot locate the tote-on-cylinder area, stop and escalate to training/support for clarification.

source_evidence.quote: “This is where the tote sits on the cylinder.”

steps.title: Confirm the tote sits on the cylinder at the tote rack
steps.purpose: Verify the physical starting condition for the centering behavior described in the source.
steps.instruction: Confirm that the tote is positioned on the cylinder at the tote rack (tote-on-cylinder positioning).
steps.expected_result: The tote is visibly seated on the cylinder at the tote rack location.
steps.healthy_condition: Tote is seated on the cylinder at the rack position.
steps.failure_condition: Tote is not seated on the cylinder at the rack position (or the seating condition cannot be confirmed).

actions.label: Confirm tote-on-cylinder positioning
actions.exact_action: Confirm the tote sits on the cylinder at the tote rack.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the tote rack area does not show the expected tote-on-cylinder seating condition, stop and escalate to training/support for clarification.

source_evidence.quote: “This is where the tote sits on the cylinder.”

steps.title: Identify the tote rack “little feet” and their centering purpose
steps.purpose: Verify the primary alignment mechanism that centers the tote when it drops.
steps.instruction: Look for the “little feet” on the tote rack and confirm they are present on the rack hardware around the tote drop position.
steps.expected_result: You can point to the rack’s “little feet” feature.
steps.healthy_condition: Little feet are visible on the tote rack and are positioned such that they align the tote to the center when the tote drops.
steps.failure_condition: The tote rack does not appear to have the described “little feet” feature.

actions.label: Locate little feet
actions.exact_action: Look for the “little feet” on the tote rack.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the tote rack does not appear to have the described little feet, stop and escalate to training/support for clarification.

source_evidence.quote: “We have little feet so that when the tote drops, it is aligned to the center.”

steps.title: Identify the tote rack side “fins” and their off-center centering purpose
steps.purpose: Verify the secondary centering mechanism that helps move packages toward center after off-center impacts.
steps.instruction: Look for the side “fins” on the tote rack and confirm they are present on the rack hardware along the sides of the tote drop area.
steps.expected_result: You can point to the rack’s side fins feature.
steps.healthy_condition: Side fins are visible and positioned to help move packages toward the center if they hit off-center.
steps.failure_condition: The tote rack does not appear to have the described side fins feature.

actions.label: Locate side fins
actions.exact_action: Look for the side “fins” on the tote rack.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the tote rack does not appear to have the described side fins, stop and escalate to training/support for clarification.

source_evidence.quote: “We also have these fins on the side that help move packages towards the center if they kind of hit.”

steps.title: Note building-specific impact severity guidance (building vs Hazlett)
steps.purpose: Set expectations for how critical the centering hardware behavior is at different sites/buildings.
steps.instruction: If comparing sites/buildings, note the source guidance that in this building it “doesn’t matter as much” because the actual drop is more severe at Hazlett, where something needs to hit against to ensure centering and reduce items on the floor.
steps.expected_result: You can state the source’s site/building guidance: this building is less sensitive; Hazlett drop severity requires centering impact behavior to reduce items on the floor.
steps.healthy_condition: Your understanding matches the described comparison: less critical here; more severe at Hazlett with centering impact needs.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot apply the building vs Hazlett guidance when asked, or you contradict the described comparison.

actions.label: Apply site/building guidance
actions.exact_action: Note the training statement about building vs Hazlett drop severity and centering impact needs.

source_evidence.quote: “Yeah, in this building it doesn't matter as much because the actual drop is much more severe where at Hazlett you need something to kind of hit against to make sure that you get into the center of the tote and you don't have a lot of items on the floor.”

success_criteria: You can identify and describe the tote rack centering mechanisms: tote sits on the cylinder; little feet align the tote to the center when it drops; side fins help move packages toward the center after off-center hits.
healthy_conditions: Tote rack shows tote-on-cylinder seating location.
Little feet are visible and associated with center alignment on tote drop.
Side fins are visible and associated with centering after off-center impacts.
failure_conditions: Tote rack does not appear to have the described little feet.
Tote rack does not appear to have the described side fins.
Tote-on-cylinder seating area cannot be confirmed.
escalation_guidance: If the tote rack does not appear to have the described little feet or side fins, stop and escalate to training/support for clarification.

screens_or_images.what_to_look_at: Tote rack/tote-on-cylinder area and the described features: little feet (center alignment on drop) and side fins (move packages toward center if they hit off-center).
